# 5-Day Budget Montreal Trip from Toronto

A low-stress, transit-first plan for 2 adults that keeps the trip under **CAD 1,200** by using a downtown hotel, a mix of museums and food, and one evening activity. Walking is kept light each day, with transit or short rides used to connect major stops.

## Trip Cost Plan for 2 Adults

| Category | Estimated Cost (CAD) | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Round-trip GO/VIA/Flix-style intercity travel | 220 | Book early for the best fare |
| Downtown hotel, 4 nights | 560 | Budget hotel near Berri-UQAM / Quartier des Spectacles |
| Transit in Montreal | 40 | 3-day STM passes or pay-per-ride mix |
| Museums and attractions | 150 | Mix of free and paid entries |
| Food and drinks | 210 | Casual breakfasts, lunches, and dinners |
| Evening activity | 40 | One low-cost night outing |
| Buffer | 30 | Small price swings |
| **Total** | **1,250** | Trim with cheaper hotel or 1 free museum day |

**Budget target adjustment:** To stay under **CAD 1,200**, aim for either:
- a hotel total closer to **CAD 500**, or
- one fewer paid attraction, or
- more meals from bakeries/cafés and grocery snacks.

## 5-Day Montreal Itinerary

### Day 1: Travel In, Old Montreal Arrival, Easy Dinner
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/train-front.svg
- Morning: Depart Toronto by intercity train or bus; bring snacks and water.
- Afternoon: Check in near downtown, then take STM to Old Montreal for a light first walk.
- Food: Casual dinner in Old Montreal or downtown brasserie.
- Estimated cost: **CAD 220 travel + 140 hotel + 60 food + 10 transit = 430**
- Transit tip: Stay near **Berri-UQAM**, **Place-des-Arts**, or **Lucien-L’Allier** for easy metro access and less walking.

### Day 2: Museum Day + Downtown Food
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Visit the **Montreal Museum of Fine Arts** or a comparable central museum.
- Afternoon: Lunch downtown, then a second museum or nearby gallery.
- Food: Budget-friendly lunch bowl, sandwich, or casual bistro meal.
- Estimated cost: **CAD 35 museum + 70 food + 10 transit = 115**
- Transit tip: Use the metro between museum and lunch areas to keep walking under 2 hours total.

### Day 3: Plateau Food Stops + Evening Activity
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- Morning: Slow breakfast, then metro to the Plateau for café and bagel stops.
- Afternoon: Browse a neighborhood market or free public spaces with short walking loops.
Media: Alt=Afternoon: Browse a neighborhood market or free public spaces with short walking loops, Montreal, Canada
- Food: Montreal bagels, café lunch, and a simple dinner.
- Evening: Low-cost activity such as a jazz bar, live music set, or scenic evening walk in the city core.
- Estimated cost: **CAD 45 food + 15 transit + 40 evening = 100**
- Transit tip: Keep this day metro-heavy and limit walking by grouping stops in the same neighborhood.

### Day 4: Old Port, Science Museum, Light Night Out
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg
- Morning: Head to the Old Port area early before crowds build.
- Afternoon: Visit the **Montreal Science Centre** or another attraction in the same zone.
- Food: Lunch near the waterfront, then a relaxed dinner downtown.
- Evening: Optional short stroll or riverside view; keep it easy after the museum day.
- Estimated cost: **CAD 25 transit + 35 attraction + 70 food = 130**
- Transit tip: Combine Old Port and science-center stops in one outing so you only make one metro/bus transfer chain.

### Day 5: Breakfast, Last Museum or Market Stop, Return to Toronto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/bag-check.svg
- Morning: Pack early, check out, then do one final short stop such as a market, bookstore, or free museum section.
- Afternoon: Eat a simple lunch and return to Toronto.
- Food: Breakfast pastries, lunch sandwiches, and travel snacks.
- Estimated cost: **CAD 25 food + 220 return travel = 245**
- Transit tip: Leave luggage at the hotel front desk or a station locker if needed so the final stop stays easy.

## Budget-Friendly Stay and Transit Tips

- Pick a hotel near **downtown Montreal** with metro access, ideally close to **Berri-UQAM**, **Place-des-Arts**, or **Guy-Concordia**.
- Use the **STM metro** for most movement; it is faster and cheaper than rideshares.
- Buy a **multi-day transit pass** only if it beats pay-per-ride for your route mix.
- Book museum tickets online when possible, and look for one **free admission window** or low-cost exhibit.
- Keep meals simple: breakfast at a bakery, lunch at a café, dinner at a casual bistro.

## Simple Packing Checklist

- Government ID and travel confirmation
- Debit/credit card and a small cash backup
- Comfortable walking shoes
- Light jacket or layer for cool evenings
- Compact umbrella or rain shell
- Phone charger and power bank
- Reusable water bottle
- Transit app and hotel address saved offline
- Small day bag
- Any personal medication
